thread:
Morgan: Heads up — production KV cache on r-infer-02 shows steady RSS increase when serving >512k token contexts. Not an immediate OOM but growth ~1.8GB/day.

Priya: How reproducible? Can you paste the short profiler snapshot?

Morgan: Repro is consistent on long-context replay job. Perf sample:

```
alloc_bytes: 1_234_567_890
free_ops: 1_200_000
slab_frag_pct: 27.4
largest_free_region: 48KB
avg_alloc_size: 1.2KB
compaction_runs: 3 (last 24h)
```

Javier: Slabbing looks bad — largest_free_region 48KB suggests lots of small holes. What's the allocator policy? buddy or slab?

Morgan: It's our hybrid slab->span allocator. We shard by block_size_class, fallback to span allocations. Observed many 1-4KB allocations from KV entries when mixing short and long sequences.

Elena: Any change after enabling aggressive reuse flag `kv_reuse_small=true`?

Morgan: Tried that with a flood test. Freed ~600MB but CPU went up 12% and tail latency spiked +40ms on 95th. Not acceptable for host-tier requests.

Tia: Could we try histogram-driven compaction — only run compaction when live_frag_histogram shows >X in tiny bins? That would avoid compaction churn on healthy heaps.

Priya: I prototyped a histogram detector last week. Basic idea: maintain per-shard histogram of free-run lengths; trigger compaction if fraction of holes <=64B exceeds 30% AND overall free < 20%. Early results: reclaimed 800MB on long runs, CPU 4% overhead avg.

Morgan: Nice. Can you share config used?

Priya: Config:

```
hist_bins = [64,128,256,512,1024,4096,16384]
trigger_small_bin_pct = 0.30
min_free_pct = 0.20
compact_budget_ms = 50
idle_grace_ms = 200
```

Javier: Compact budget 50ms per cycle — that might increase latencies if done inline. We should offload to background worker with low-priority scheduling and pause on tail events.

Elena: Also wondering about paging interaction — when we run compaction we touch lots of pages and cause paging spikes. Any tl;dr on page faults?

Morgan: Yes, observed pagefault bursts during compaction; spike in pss and io. That's why we capped budget. Background worker with page-friendly shuffling (use `madvise` to prefetch?) could help.

Tia: Could we try "staged compaction": first merge buddy runs within same page boundaries to reduce page faults, then do cross-page merges slowly.

Priya: Agreed. Also propose adding per-alloc-class freelist warming: when free runs exceed threshold, pre-merge into larger blocks to service long allocations without spans.

Javier: Planning an experiment: enable histogram detector + background staged compaction on a canary pool for 48h. Metrics to watch: rss, p95 latency, compaction CPU, page-faults/sec, freed_bytes. Rollback if p95 > baseline + 25ms or freed_bytes < 200MB.

Morgan: I'll spin up canary tomorrow. @infra-bot please schedule canary with config branch kv/hist-compaction-v1.

infra-bot: scheduled canary r-infer-canary-3 -> kv/hist-compaction-v1, start 2026-03-20T02:00Z

Elena: Also add tracepoint around kv-alloc/free to sample fragmentation heatmap every 10s.

Priya: Will push a small probe and dashboard panels.

Morgan: Thanks. If results look promising, followups: (1) evaluate different block_sizes, (2) try lazy compaction on eviction time (compact before evicting to avoid small-span leaks), (3) integrate with batching heuristics to avoid compactions during high throughput windows.

Javier: +1. Document the rollback plan and add circuit-breaker to disable compaction if CPU > 75%.

Tia: Suggest adding a synthetic long-context workload to CI so regression doesn't slip.

Morgan: Agreed. I'll create the ticket with links to profiles. Thanks all :thumbsup:

infra-bot: created ticket INF-2041: "kv: histogram-triggered compaction + staged merges" -> https://tracker.redwood.ai/INF-2041
